script: He diagnosed Stalin with paranoia, and was dead the next day. In 1927, the Soviet Union's top neurologist examined Stalin privately at the Kremlin. He walked out and told colleagues exactly what he found: a paranoiac with a withered arm. By the next morning, he was dead. Only his brain was examined, and his body was cremated the same day. Soviet authorities erased his name from every medical textbook until Stalin himself died decades later. Officials called it natural causes. Nobody who knew him believed that for a second. He diagnosed Stalin with paranoia, and paid for it within a day.
